# Adapted from PR-Agent

The files in this directory started as copies of parts of [PR-Agent](https://github.com/the-pr-agent/pr-agent) 0.50.0, taken so that the `pr-agent` package and everything it pulls in no longer have to be installed. They have since been modified here and are maintained as this project's own code. PR-Agent is MIT licensed; its copyright and permission notice is in `LICENSE.pr-agent` and is installed with the package.

| File | Started from, in PR-Agent 0.50.0 | Changed here |
|---|---|---|
| `patch.py` | `to_hunk_only_patch` and `decouple_and_convert_to_hunks_with_lines_numbers` with its helpers, from `pr_agent/algo/git_patch_processing.py`, and `FilePatchInfo` and `EDIT_TYPE` from `pr_agent/algo/types.py` | The numbered hunk text (`numbered`) is built from the unidiff hunks the citable lines come from, instead of from a second parse of the patch, so every line a finding may cite is shown once with its head line number. Hunk headers are shown with both counts. A blank context line and a context-only hunk are shown like any other. A line break other than a line feed inside a line is shown as a space. The trim splits on line feeds only. `FilePatchInfo`, `EDIT_TYPE` and the hunk header parsing are gone, and nothing about the change under review is logged. |
| `pr_review_prompt.system.txt` | `pr_review_prompt.system` in `pr_agent/settings/pr_reviewer_prompts.toml`, rendered for this reviewer | Asks for a JSON object holding only `review.key_issues_to_review`, and the `relevant_code` quote the prompt asks for, instead of fenced YAML with fields nothing reads. Names as untrusted the inputs the prompt carries. Describes the hunk format as it is shown, and what scanner evidence is. The guidance on what to flag and how to write it is PR-Agent's. The finding limit is left as `__MAX_FINDINGS__`. |
| `tokens.py` | The choice of encoding in `TokenEncoder._create_encoder`, and its pointing tiktoken at bundled files | The two encoding files are bundled here and checked against tiktoken's published SHA-256 before first use. Only an unknown model name falls back to `o200k_base`; a file that cannot be read is an error. |
| `tiktoken/` | `cl100k_base` and `o200k_base`, the encoding files LiteLLM bundles and PR-Agent points tiktoken at | Unchanged, under the names tiktoken's cache gives them |

`tiktoken/` holds two public data files from OpenAI's tiktoken distribution. tiktoken is pointed at this directory unless `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR` or `DATA_GYM_CACHE_DIR` is already set. Without them a fresh container downloads both files from the internet before its first review, and the offline test run in the image fails.

`tests/test_vendor.py` pins the rendered rubric by hash, checks that it asks for the fields `parse_answer` reads, checks that the hunk text numbers exactly the lines unidiff numbers, and pins the trim against PR-Agent's output. The rubric is named by its hash in `engine.review`'s cache signature, so a changed rubric is never served an answer cached with an earlier one.
